strategy.summary:
Edelstahl-Service Donautal is a sound, group-owned stainless stockholder and our main source (80% quota) for round bar 1.4404 (part:370010). It is cheaper than the second source sup:70740, and we are a small customer to it. The framework contract ctr:4600070710 already carries a 45% AS-14404 index clause with quarterly adjustment. It runs to year end and auto-renews unless notice is given within the window (#8.1). The supplier now asks to agree the price basis for the coming period with an AS-14404 clause (doc:20260912-70710-P08). By its own letter, however, its nickel and alloys are bought at fixed prices until March 2027 (doc:20260706-70710-M1). An index rise therefore does not reach its cost before then. The owner has offered an open calculation (doc:20260421-70710-M2).

Our position:
- Strongest lever: its hedge admission, combined with the recent fall in the alloy surcharge.
- Weakness: there is no credible exit on price, because the rival is dearer and Donautal's 2026-09-19 small-volume RFQ quote is far above its renewal quote.

Approach: anchor moderately, trade the index start date, contract length and volume, and keep it as a healthy partner. Part 370021 (sheet 1.4301, currently 100% with sup:70730) is a possible bundling carrot.
strategy.decision_maker: The owner/managing director, who is personally involved and offered the open-book calculation (doc:20260421-70710-M2). Group approval behind him is unknown; the evidence on approvals is thin.

Its plant shuts over the turn of the year, and January call-offs are needed early.

trades.why: It insists on a clause. Accept its own AS-14404 clause with no deadband, but with the base or start aligned to its hedge expiry and in exchange for a lower base price. Do not offer a generous clause on a rising index.
A 24-month commitment gives it planning security and is worth price. 36 months is not worth more than 24.
The shared forecast is stable and reliable, so a binding volume within our need is low-risk for us and valued by it.
The hedge runs into spring. Any increase should start only after that; offer later-date-at-slightly-higher-price alternatives.
It shows no cash need, and the current terms are already short. Test longer payment cheaply only if it is offered free.
Recurring mixed defects; do not give it away without a return.

price_view.reasoning: There is no should-cost, so margin is unknown; the evidence is thin. Its renewal quote holds the current price until its hedge ends. The 12-month driver rise is largely already in the price through this year's index steps, and the alloy has eased since June. On the other side, the cold-drawing PPI rise gives it a checkable case for an increase. The rival is dearer, so we have no price threat. Realistic aim: hold the current price through the hedge period, perhaps a small cut against a volume and length trade, and defer clause effects. It is sound, so squeezing would not harm its health, but it can walk away and we would fall back on a dearer source.

strategy.writer_notes: Lead with its own hedge letter and the open-book offer. Frame our position as fair: the price stays as quoted while its material is fixed, and any clause starts only when its hedge ends, with a sound base. Offer length and binding volume as the trades for that. Mention a possible role on the sheet part only if a bundle case arises. Keep each e-mail short and formal, cite record IDs, and keep one fresh fact back for each round.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for either part, so the margin over full cost cannot be measured; the owner offered to walk us through hourly rates and material, which is the only route to a cost breakdown. The evidence on margin is thin.

370010 round bar 1.4404: the current price is 5.45 (since 2026-07-01, +0.4%). This is -13.8% since 2023 but +4.0% over the 2025-Q4 low of 5.17. The weighted 12-month driver change is about +7% (AS-14404 +5.9% x0.43, PPI-C2431 +12.3% x0.36, LCI +2.7% x0.03). The 2026 index steps already passed through about +5.4% (5.17 to 5.45), so most of the driver rise is already in the price.

The alloy surcharge AS-14404 has fallen -5.5% since 2026-06, and the supplier says its nickel and alloys are bought at fixed prices until March 2027. Its material cost will therefore not rise before Q2 2027. Any increase before then, or the next quarterly index step, is unsupported by its actual costs. If the clause is kept, the Q4 index adjustment should go down.

Its two quotes for 370010 contradict each other. The renewal quote is 5.45 (2026-09-10, material covered until March 2027). The second-source RFQ quote is 6.31 (2026-09-19, at only 23,700 per year). The 6.31 looks like a small-volume or opportunistic price and must not become the anchor.

The rival for 370010 is dearer. Blankstahl Werdenfels quoted 6.06 and we buy from it at 5.84 (+11% index step in 2026-Q3), both above Donautal's 5.45. In 2025 Donautal won the benchmark at 5.34 against 5.41. Competitive pressure on Donautal's 370010 price is weak; do not reveal the rival prices.

370021 sheet 1.4301: Donautal is not the current source (Inox Center Ostalpen, 100% quota, 4.05). Donautal's last quote was 4.29 in 2024, a tie, which it lost. Drivers rose about +6.3% weighted in 12 months, but AS-14301 is -7.6% since 2026-06 and -17.6% from its 2023 peak. Any Donautal bid must beat 4.05 to win.

Room on price for 370010: hold at 5.45 with no step until 2027-03. A 1-2% cut can be argued from the recent alloy fall and the hedge. Its renewal pattern has settled 3.1 percentage points below its ask on average.

findings.text: Their nickel/alloy requirement is hedged at fixed prices until March 2027 (own admission, letter 2026-07-06). Any AS-14404 rise (+5.9% in 12 months) does not reach their cost before then. This undercuts both a price increase and their new request for an index clause on part:370010.

On 2026-09-12 they asked to agree the price basis for the coming period including an AS-14404 adjustment clause for part:370010. Their aim is to pass alloy movements through. The contract already has a 45% AS-14404 clause (#3.2), so their letter likely aims to keep or widen that clause. Since their own material cost is fixed until 03/2027, an index for 2027 would pay them for costs they do not have. We could offer a fixed price, or an index starting only from April 2027.

The owner is personally involved and offered openness: on the 2026-04-21 call he offered to walk us through their calculation (hourly rates and material). The decision-maker is reachable and receptive to a fact-based cost discussion. Accepting a cost breakdown (open-book) would expose that the material is hedged. Their tone in letters is formal and short.

The supplier is financially sound and not under stress: €165M turnover, 350 staff, group-owned, equity ratio 33.9%, credit index 177 (unchanged on a year ago), VDA 6.3 audit grade A, ISO 9001/14001. We are a small customer to them (~0.3% of turnover). They can afford to walk away, and they do not urgently need cash.

We pay reliably: average 1.9 days after due over the last 12 months, never more than 7 days late, no discount abuse. We are a fair customer, though 78.7% of invoices are paid slightly late. They have voiced no cash complaints in the evidence.
Operational sensitivity: plant closed 23 Dec–6 Jan, and January call-offs are needed by 10 Dec. Respecting this signals good partnership around the year-end price talks.
The news item is trade-fair noise and offers no lever. The evidence on persona and approvals is thin beyond the owner contact.

findings.text: Framework agreement for part:370010 runs to 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice, so the deadline to stop the renewal is 2026-11-01. That gives us a credible exit window now. Prices are fixed per calendar year; a change needs written notice at least 60 days before year end (by ~2026-11-01).

The contract already contains an AS-14404 index clause: 45% material share, zero deadband, quarterly adjustment. The supplier's 2026-09-12 letter asking to 'agree a price adjustment clause based on AS-14404' therefore asks for something largely in place. It may want a higher share or a new base. Its own letter says nickel and alloys are bought at fixed prices until March 2027, so index rises do not reach its cost before then. A full pass-through plus a base-price increase would double-count.

Other terms are payment 30 days net (our standard is 60, so this is already a concession to them), DAP, 10-day lead time, a 95% OTD target and a EUR 150 flat fee per complaint. OTD runs at 88%, below the contractual 95%. Seven complaints cost EUR 1,050 in recharges, and one 8D is still open.

Renewal history shows it settles well below its ask:
- 2023-11: asked -3.1%, settled -7.1%
- 2024-12: asked +2%, settled -1.5%
- 2025-12: asked +3.2%, settled +1.4%

The average gap is about 3.1 pp, though the gap narrowed last year. Price fell from 6.06–6.61 (2023) to 5.45 now.

Dependency is mutual but asymmetric. We are 0.3% of its turnover, and it is financially sound (equity 33.9%, stable credit index). We hold 80% of part:370010 with it, but sup:70740 is active at 20%, so we can shift quota. However, 70740 is dearer: EUR 5.84 on orders and a 6.06 quote, versus 5.45 here. Two second-source benchmark RFQs (rfq:6000000208, rfq:6000000218) are open. No tooling is involved (tooling_owner n/a), so switching cost is low; the library's tooling arguments contradict the sourcing data.
On part:370021 this supplier is qualified at 0% quota; sup:70730 holds 100% at 4.05. This is a possible bundling carrot: offering volume on 370021 in exchange for terms on 370010.

findings.text: Delivery is middling and flat: 88.0% on time vs requested date in the 12 months to 2026-09 (92% vs its own confirmed date), unchanged from a year earlier and below the contractual 95% target. When late, it is 14 days late on average (max 21), which is long against a 10-day standard lead time. Still above the peer median of 84.6%. The scorecard trend rose from 82.1% (2024Q4) to a 92% peak (2026Q1), then fell back to 88%.

Quality is good by peer standards: 75 ppm rolling against a peer median of 457 ppm, no overdue 8Ds, VDA 6.3 grade A, class A green. However, complaints are steady at 7-9 per year and spread over many defect types (porosity, leakage, missing marking, burr). This points to process discipline issues rather than one root cause. Missing marking recurs 5 times. The rolling-12-month figures, which feed the quality_record argument, favour the supplier; only the complaint count is a mild lever for us. The latest QN (qn:20005016, 2026-09-06) has no closed 8D yet. EUR 2,550 has been recharged in total under the EUR 150 flat fee, and several QNs were not recharged.

It is our main source for part:370010 (quota 80%, about 93 t a year). Its price is EUR 5.45, below the second source sup:70740 at EUR 5.84 and that supplier's quote of 6.06. Its prices are already 10% below 2023. The supplier therefore has a credible case that it is the cheap, reliable option.

The volume outlook is stable to slightly up: 118.5 t forecast for the next 12 months vs 116.3 t ordered in the last 12 months. Forecasts are shared and have proven accurate (orders track forecasts within a few %). This makes a binding volume commitment low-risk for us and a tradeable good for them. Our spend is only about 0.3% of its turnover. Seasonal dips (Dec, Aug) match its plant closure.

part:370021: we buy nothing from this supplier (quota 0%, qualified only). The current source sup:70730 is at EUR 4.05. This gives a bundling opportunity: volume of about 72 t to offer in exchange for concessions on 370010.

arguments.text: Our price is the lowest on the table. Blankstahl Werdenfels has been at 5.84 since July (+11 % index step) and quoted 6.06 in the September benchmark. Our 5.45 holds for 90 days and, given our material cover, effectively until March 2027. We are already giving Hollerau stability; we are not asking for an increase.

Conversion costs have risen and are not hedged. Producer prices for cold drawing of bars are +12.3 % in 12 months, and manufacturing labour costs are +2.7 %. Since the 2026 renewal we have absorbed most of that; the 2026 index steps only passed on the alloy share. There is no case for a cut.

Alloy is rising again, not falling. The AS-14404 alloy surcharge stands at EUR 3,008/t, +6 % year on year, and the low is behind us. The 45 % index clause already in our framework contract is the fair, symmetric mechanism, and it has given Hollerau cuts in 7 of 12 quarters. We only ask to keep it for the coming period.
The price has already fallen sharply over the relationship. It went from 6.32 to 5.45 (about -14 %), with renewal cuts of -7.1 % and -1.5 % given in 2024 and 2025. We have been a fair partner.

Delivery is improving. On-time delivery against the confirmed date is 92 % over the last 12 months, the scorecard is class A green at 93.6, and no 8D report is overdue. Our 10-day lead time beats Blankstahl's 14 days.
Our books are open. Our owner offered to walk Hollerau through the hourly rates and material calculation.

weak_points: Our own letter says nickel and alloys are bought at fixed prices until March 2027. An index rise does not reach our cost before then, so a clause starting in January would be a windfall.
Our 6.31 quote for 23,700 kg (rfq:6000000218) looks opportunistic next to 5.45, and they may read it as our real margin room.

Quality: 23 supplier-caused complaints and a recurring missing-marking defect, with leakage up again in 2026 (4 complaints from April to June). The 8D for qn:20005016 is still open, and ppm went back up to 75.
On-time delivery against the requested date is only 88 % versus the 95 % target in clause 6.1, with an average of 14 days late when late.
We are sound (equity 33.9 %, credit index stable) and Hollerau is under 0.5 % of our turnover, so we cannot plead hardship.
Alloy surcharge fell 5.5 % from its June level, and electricity is -43 % versus 2022.

red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the partnership and the improved scorecard. Confirm that we hold 5.45 through Q1 2027 thanks to our material cover. Propose to continue the existing AS-14404 clause with its first adjustment in April 2027 and a 24-month term at forecast volume, while noting the +12 % cold-drawing cost we are absorbing. Offer the owner's open calculation, and signal interest in quoting the 1.4301 sheet as part of a bundle.

rebuttals.answer: We value that your renewal quote holds today's price, and we acknowledge it is competitive. Holding the price is consistent with your own letter that material is covered at fixed prices into next spring: your material cost does not move before then, so a stable price is the fair reflection of your cost, not an extra concession. We would like to build on it: a longer commitment and a binding volume in exchange for this price basis, with any adjustment starting only when your cover ends.

We accept that conversion and labour costs have risen and are not hedged. In proportion, labour is a very small share of this bar, and the cold-drawing index has eased from its recent level. Your renewal quote already keeps today's price, which shows these costs are covered. Rather than weigh general indices against each other, we would gladly take up your owner's offer to walk us through the actual calculation, so we agree on the real drivers together.

We agree the clause in our framework is a fair, symmetric mechanism, and we are willing to keep it. The surcharge has fallen noticeably since June, so the trend is not one-way. More importantly, your alloys are bought at fixed prices until next spring, so index moves do not reach your cost before then. We therefore propose to keep your clause, with no deadband, but with its base and start aligned to the end of your material cover, so neither side gains a windfall.

You have been a fair partner and we recognise it. Most of that past decline came through the index clause following the alloy market down, which is exactly the mechanism working as agreed, rather than discretionary cuts. Renewals have also tended to settle close to market movements. We see the history as proof the formula works, and want to continue on that basis.

Measured against our requested dates, however, on-time delivery is still below the target in our quality agreement, and late deliveries run long. Complaints also recur in the same defect types. We would like to agree a joint improvement plan and keep the agreed complaint fee in place as part of the new period.

We appreciate the offer and would like to accept it with thanks. A shared look at material and processing costs, including the fixed material cover, is the best basis for agreeing both the price and the start of the adjustment clause.

press: As your material is covered at fixed prices until next spring, we suggest the adjustment clause takes its base and starts only when that cover ends.

The alloy surcharge has eased since June, which we would like reflected in the next quarterly step under the existing clause.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement fixes prices for each calendar year.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070710#3.1 (price): Prices as per the price annex, fixed for each calendar year. Changes require written notice of at least 60 days before the end of the calendar year.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement ties the price to an agreed index formula.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070710#3.2 (index): The price follows index AS-14404: P = P0 x (1 - 0.45 + 0.45 x I(m-2) / I(base)), base = the index two months before the price year starts, adjusted quarterly on the 1st of January, April, July and October if the change exceeds 0 %. The series moved +5.9% in 12 months.
